label: Encoding phase from 3rd original token through <DEL>
explanation: Positional/phase feature: fires on every original-phase step from the third original token (t=2) onward and on the <DEL> delimiter step, i.e. (t >= 2) & (t <= L). Never fires at t=0 or t=1, and is essentially silent during the copy phase (0.4% of copy steps, 0.1% of mass). Token identity of the current input has little effect (rate ~0.35-0.36 for every letter). Within a sequence activation tends to ramp up across the original tokens and peaks at <DEL> (delimiter step: 94% active, 29% of mass); the strongest examples start with tokens like i/g followed by c. Activation rate in the original phase falls at late positions (t=9 rate 0.18), and repeated tokens (in_first=0) fire less often. Dev F1 0.96, mass recall 0.999.

issues: The predicate and label hold up. Test scores reproduce: precision 0.927, recall 0.996, F1 0.960, mass recall 0.999. Coverage by activation quartile is 0.985-1.000. Missed activations are scattered weak copy-phase firings that carry 0.1% of the mass. I found no systematic false-positive class: precision stays between 0.90 and 0.96 when split by orig(0)==orig(1), a digit in orig(0) or orig(1), n_digits>=3, t==2, L==3 and L==9.

The claim 'firing rate drops at late original positions (0.18 at t=9)' is false. It mixes up t with phase. Inside the original phase, the rate by orig_idx is 0.90/0.91/0.92/0.95/0.97/0.96/0.90 for idx 2-8. The per-t drop (0.18 at t=9) appears only because for short L, large t falls in the copy phase.

The claim 'a token that has already appeared earlier (in_first=0) fires less often' is false. On the dev split for (t>=2)&(t<L), precision is 0.934 when in_first==0 and 0.923 when in_first==1, so repeated tokens fire slightly more often.

The claim 'every letter has an activation rate of about 0.35-0.36' is misleading. Those rates are taken over all steps, copy phase included, so they mostly reflect phase. Inside the predicate region the feature fires about 90%+ of the time whatever the token. The underlying point (token identity barely matters) is correct.
The phase claims check out: no firing at t=0 or t=1, delimiter 94% active with 29% of the mass, copy phase 0.4% active with 0.1% of the mass.
